stem:
Parth colours a $4$-by-$4$ grid in checkerboard black and white, then removes two white corner squares. He wants to cover the remaining region with $2 \times 1$ tiles that do not overlap and leave no gaps.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: The remaining region has even area $14$, so it can be tiled by $2 \times 1$ tiles.
Every $2 \times 1$ tile covers one black square and one white square.
The remaining region has $8$ black squares and $6$ white squares, so it cannot be tiled by $2 \times 1$ tiles.
Only the total number of squares matters for tiling with $2 \times 1$ tiles.

teacher.key_rationale: A 4×4 checkerboard has 8 black and 8 white; removing two white corners leaves 8 black and 6 white. Each 2×1 tile covers one of each colour, so unequal counts block a tiling even though area 14 is even. Even area alone, or ignoring colour, misses the invariant.
